deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematical derivation on this page. It is a draft of qualitative physiological reasoning for Riemann's posthumous fragment 'Mechanik des Ohres' (bundle R.Ohr). It continues the argument of the previous page: the middle-ear apparatus must pass pressure changes to the labyrinth fluid in a constant, or only slowly varying, ratio. Riemann therefore looks for disturbances that could slowly change the geometry of the apparatus. This page takes up two of them: temperature, and the position of the ossicles.

(a) Top block, marked 'vgl. p. 9' (compare p. 9). The 'Gesetz' (law) it refers to was evidently stated on p. 9. Under that law one cannot infer a part's temperature changes from its temperature. Individual temperatures can no more be fixed exactly than the temperature changes can be estimated.

(b) Point 1), on cooling of the external auditory canal (Gehörgang), reading uncertain. Air in the canal is a poor conductor and radiator of heat. Cool air keeps entering at the opening of the canal. So the canal air sits at a lower temperature than the surrounding tissue and cartilage, and cools the tympanic cavity (Paukenhöhle) through the eardrum.
- The Eustachian tube (tuba) exchanges air with the tympanic cavity only occasionally, not with ordinary breathing. So no regular, strong cooling can be attributed to it.
- Conclusion: there is no strong, constant cooling of the tympanic cavity. Hence its temperature should not depart noticeably from body temperature.
- A second point 2) begins 'dagegen ist die Pyramiden…' (perhaps the pyramidal eminence or petrous pyramid, which houses the stapedius) but breaks off. An insertion 'als die der Paukenhöhle' ('than that of the tympanic cavity') sits above the next block.

(c) Block marked 'pag. 25', on kinematics of the ossicular chain.
- The position of the lenticular bone (Linsenbein, os lenticulare / processus lenticularis of the incus) relative to the oval window cannot stay unchanged.
- But rotating the incus about its fixed suspension point can make the lenticular process move only parallel to one direction of the window. Then the stapes needs to rotate about the incudostapedial joint only in that single direction to keep its footplate seated in the oval window.
- A muscle, the M. stapedius, exists to rotate the stapes about that joint in this direction only, not in the perpendicular one. Riemann infers that rotation in the perpendicular direction is made unnecessary by the incus joint being held in the same position.
- The closing paragraph is struck out. It concerned testing these assumptions against experience.

In modern terms, all of this is a degrees-of-freedom argument. The footplate is a constrained body, so the motion of the incus-stapes joint is restricted to one direction. One muscle then suffices for one rotational correction. No equations are written.
errors: Physiologically the claim is plausible for its time: the middle ear stays near body temperature, and the stapedius acts as a stabilizer and tilter of the stapes. The idea that the ossicle geometry reduces the needed correction to one direction is speculative, but not in error.
Point 2) is left unfinished, and the final paragraph is cancelled, so the argument on this page is incomplete.

results.what: Argument that the tympanic cavity temperature stays close to body temperature: the air in the external canal is a poor heat conductor, and the Eustachian tube ventilates only occasionally. This rules out thermal drift of the transmission apparatus.
results.modern_name: Thermal stability of the middle ear (qualitative)

results.what: Kinematic argument: rotating the incus about its suspension point confines the motion of the lenticular process to one direction. So only one stapes rotation, supplied by the stapedius muscle, is needed to keep the footplate seated in the oval window.
results.modern_name: Ossicular chain kinematics / function of the stapedius muscle
results.usually_credited_to: Helmholtz (1868, Die Mechanik der Gehörknöchelchen) and anatomists such as Henle; Riemann's fragment 'Mechanik des Ohres' was published 1867 by Henle

deep.surprise_reason: These are draft passages of Riemann's known, posthumously published ear-mechanics fragment. The content is qualitative physiology with no new mathematics. The details on temperature and the stapedius are minor unpublished draft material.
transcription_corrections: 'Vorhofsknochen' should probably read 'Vorhofsfenster' (oval window), in 'Die Lage des Linsenbeins gegen das Vorhofsfenster' and 'parallel ... des Vorhofsfensters'.
Line 1 likely ends 'nicht auf dessen Temperaturänderungen schließen' rather than 'Temperatur oder gar schließen'.
Point 1) likely begins 'Was die Abkühlung des äußeren Gehörganges betrifft', not 'Ausbildung'.
'Wärme-Leiter und Wärmespeicher' may be 'Wärmeleiter und -strahler'; reading uncertain.
'Pyramidenhöhle' in the unfinished point 2) is uncertain; it may refer to the pyramidal eminence or the petrous pyramid.
